name: LME49721 (National / TI low-voltage rail-to-rail I/O audio dual)
tagline: A rare audio-grade rail-to-rail I/O dual for 2.2-5.5 V supplies (4 nV/rtHz, 0.00008% THD+N). Japanese low-voltage headphone-amp builders often choose it.
technology: Dual op-amp with CMOS-type input (input bias current 40 fA typ), rail-to-rail input and output, 2.2-5.5 V single supply, 20 MHz GBW, +/-8.5 V/us slew, +/-9.7 mA output current. Only SOIC-8 (MA) ordering codes are listed.

lineage.notes: Released in the LME audio op-amp line (siblings: LME49720, LME49710). The TI datasheet header gives the origination date as September 2007, and a National copy is dated October 2007.
Acquired with National in 2011. In April 2013 the datasheet was reissued in TI format as SNAS371C. The /NOPB SOIC-8 codes are still sold.

reputation.summary: Among Japanese builders of low-voltage and portable headphone amps it is treated as a standard choice. nabe's blog (高品質な低電圧ヘッドホンアンプ) recommends it after low-voltage testing, as one of two parts alongside the AD8656. A zigsow user review is titled '高性能な低電圧駆動可能なオペアンプ…らしい。実際優秀。' ('Supposedly a high-performance low-voltage op-amp... and it really is excellent'). Akizuki sells it as a '2回路フルスイングHiFiオペアンプ' ('2-circuit full-swing HiFi op-amp'). The praise comes mostly from these Japanese hobbyist sources and is not widespread in Western audiophile forums.
typical_uses: USB-bus-powered (5 V) audio buffers and preamps
Low-voltage single-supply audio signal paths needing rail-to-rail swing
caveats: The supply is limited to 5.5 V total, so it cannot go into +/-15 V or +/-12 V sockets meant for NE5532 or OPA2134 class parts, which would destroy it.
Output current is only about +/-9.7 mA, which limits direct drive of low-impedance headphones.
Only SOIC-8 ordering codes are listed, so DIP-8 use needs an adapter.
Praise is attributed to a small number of Japanese hobbyist sources.

revision_history.changes: Initial release. The TI header gives the origination date as SEPTEMBER 2007, and the National copy is dated October 2007.
Changed the layout of the National data sheet to TI format.

counterfeit_notes: No LME49721-specific counterfeit or remark reports were found. TI lists only SOIC-8 (MA) ordering codes, so any 'LME49721' sold as a native DIP-8 is either an adapter board or suspect. Buy from authorized distributors (TI, DigiKey, Mouser).
alternatives: AD8656 (recommended alongside it on nabe's low-voltage headphone-amp tests)
OPA2365 (TI 2.2-5.5 V rail-to-rail I/O dual; editorial suggestion)
LME49720 (higher-voltage sibling from the same line; not rail-to-rail, needs larger supplies)
open_questions: Dates and change lists for SNAS371A and SNAS371B (between the 2007 National release and rev C in April 2013) were not found.
Which revision each mirror (Octopart National/TI copies, alldatasheet 538445/538446/2194639, datasheet4u, radiolocman) actually holds.
No PCN or fab/die transfer was found after the TI acquisition. Worth checking TI PCN listings for LME49721.
The lifecycle status of the legacy non-NOPB codes LME49721MA and LME49721MAX, and an explicit TI status flag for LME49721MA/NOPB.
Exact test conditions for THD+N (gain, supply, frequency) and whether quiescent current is per amplifier or total.

corrections: Channel count corrected from 0 to 2 for all part numbers (dual op-amp).
Added the /NOPB ordering codes LME49721MA/NOPB and LME49721MAX/NOPB. MAX/NOPB is marked active per Octopart, and MA/NOPB as probably active.
Reclassified LME49721MA and LME49721MAX as legacy National non-NOPB codes with unknown status.
Technology line: the vague 'fA range' bias current is replaced by the confirmed 40 fA typ, and the +/-9.7 mA output current is added.
Filled in the empty datasheets, key_specs, revision_history, lineage, ti_literature_numbers (SNAS371, SNAA051) and archive_seed_urls.
No silicon changes or revision hazards were found. silicon_changes stays empty (discovery hints were empty as well).
claims_confirmed: The current TI datasheet is SNAS371C, 'SEPTEMBER 2007-REVISED APRIL 2013' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lme49721.pdf).
Rev C (04/04/13) changed the layout of the National data sheet to TI format (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/snas371c/snas371c.pdf, via search summary).
A National-era datasheet copy dated October 2007 exists (https://www.pken.net/ish_mm/datasheet/ns/lme49721.pdf).

Specs: 2.2-5.5 V supply, 4 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz, 20 MHz GBW, +/-8.5 V/us, THD+N 0.00008% at RL = 2 kOhm, 40 fA input bias current, 2.15 mA quiescent current, +/-9.7 mA output, 118 dB AOL at 600 Ohm, 0.3 mV Vos, 103 dB PSRR (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lme49721.pdf; https://datasheet.octopart.com/LME49721MA/NOPB-National-Semiconductor-datasheet-9809305.pdf).
TI part-details pages exist for LME49721MA/NOPB and LME49721MAX/NOPB (https://www.ti.com/product/LME49721/part-details/LME49721MA/NOPB).
AN-1767 LME49721 Evaluation Board is TI document SNAA051 Rev A (https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/snaa051).
